subject: Phase-in commit smoothing & staged-billing amendment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@skylarkhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Phase-in commit proposal for upcoming renewal

Hi Alec —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together a pragmatic proposal to smooth Skylark's renewal from a seasonal spend profile into a multi‑year commit that reduces unit cost while preserving monthly cadence for your teams. High level: 

- Term: 24 months, start 2027-01-01
- Commit profile: Year 1: 60% of peak expected monthly tokens averaged across last 6 months; Year 2: 100% of peak (phased increase)
- Billing: monthly invoices based on committed units with a quarterly true‑up; optional frontloaded credits to offset Q1 ramp impact
- Auto‑renew: opt‑in on final signature with 60‑day notice for changes

I attached a simple model (forecast_model.xlsx) showing how the phased commit impacts monthly spend and per‑token effective price under three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). Key asks from Skylark: whether we can co‑term this renewal with your other Redwood contracts and whether we can offer a one‑time migration credit to offset integration work.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm whether co‑terming with the Data Platform contract is required.
2) If yes, we’ll produce a redline of the amendment and a staged invoice schedule for legal and procurement.
3) If you want the migration credit, confirm amount (we can do a one‑time $40k credit applied across first two invoices).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Legal and Finance to get the amendment drafted.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0142

Attachment: forecast_model.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Alec Turner <alec.turner@skylarkhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@skylarkhealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phase-in commit proposal for upcoming renewal

Rachel —

Appreciate the write‑up and the model. A few questions from procurement and finance: 

- Co‑terming: We do prefer co‑terming with our Data Platform contract to simplify forecasting, so yes — co‑term is preferred.
- Migration credit: $40k is reasonable but I need a confirmation that it can be amortized across invoices and shown as a line item.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices are required, but our treasury would like a maximum two‑invoice true‑up lag (i.e., true‑ups quarterly with any adjustments applied within the following month).

Two items for legal: any change to auto‑renew needs explicit opt‑out language for our side; also we prefer a 90‑day notice window (not 60). I’m CC’ing legal for visibility.

Can you confirm the staged invoice schedule and share a redlined amendment we can circulate?

Thanks,
Alec Turner
Head of Procurement — Skylark Health
alec.turner@skylarkhealth.com

Alec, Rachel —

Thanks for the clarity. From a finance perspective we can accommodate the requests with the following adjustments: 

- Co‑terming: Accepted. We'll align contract effective dates to match the Data Platform contract (we’ll need the exact co‑term end date — can you share?).
- Migration credit: We can provide a $40,000 credit that is applied as a negative invoice line across the first two monthly invoices (i.e., $20k each). We will show it as an explicit line item — acceptable for audit.
- True‑up cadence: Quarterly true‑ups with adjustments processed on the following invoice (within one month) — we can commit to that SLA.
- Auto‑renew: We can extend notice window to 90 days for Skylark. We’ll surface opt‑out language in the amendment.

I attached a quick forecast with adjusted cashflow to show the effect of amortizing the credit and the quarterly true‑up (forecast_model.xlsx).

If Alec can share the exact co‑term target date and whether Skylark expects headcount-driven burst months (Q4 heavy), we’ll bake that into our invoice ladder.

—Vivek

Alec / Skylark Legal —

Thanks — we’ve incorporated your asks and prepared a draft amendment and invoice ladder for co‑terming. Attached: contract_redlines.pdf (high‑level amendment with tracked changes) and an invoice schedule showing monthly invoices with quarterly true‑ups and the $20k credit applied to the first two invoices. Highlights: 

- Effective date aligned to 2027‑01‑01 with co‑term target of 2029‑12‑31 (matches the Data Platform end date you referenced in our earlier notes). Please confirm if that date is final.
- True‑up process: Quarter close → adjustment applied to next invoice (within 30 days).
- Auto‑renew: 90‑day notice window; explicit opt‑out clause language included.
- Term pricing: Year 1 phased uplift to reach commit in month 13; Year 2 full commit pricing tier applies thereafter.

Next steps: if legal is comfortable, we can push the redlines to DocuSign. If you prefer, we can also route through your procurement system first.

If you confirm co‑term end date and signoff on the migration credit treatment, I’ll send the DocuSign link this afternoon.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
